blocking.section: CI stages (Figure 3) and Commits and pull requests (Pull request rules)
blocking.issue: Stage 1 includes the approval count, which fails until the required approvals exist. The new Figure 3 caption and edges make stages 2 to 10 depend on stage 1. On a pull request that touches `api/`, `pkg/`, `docs/_meta/`, `go.mod` or a security-sensitive package, stage 1 stays red until the second approval, so lint, generate, build, unit, supply-chain, docs, Console, integration and gate jobs are all skipped. Reviewers then approve without CI results. Because stage 1 also reruns on each review, each approval either reruns the whole 10 plus 30 minute (target) pipeline, or reruns only stage 1 and leaves the dependent checks skipped. As drawn, the pipeline cannot give reviewers CI evidence before approval on the most sensitive paths.
blocking.evidence: Line 451 (stage 1): "DCO sign-off on the pull request's own commits, also on merge queue runs; Conventional Commits title; approval count; repocheck with the no-license-check scan". Line 467: "*Figure 3: CI stages by pipeline; stages 2 to 10 run in parallel after stage 1.*" Lines 487-495: "s1 --> s2" ... "s1 --> s10". Line 439: "two, counted by stage 1 (rerun on each review), for `api/`, `pkg/`, `docs/_meta/`, security-sensitive packages and `go.mod`".
blocking.fix: Separate the approval count from the dependency chain. Change the caption to "*Figure 3: CI stages by pipeline; stages 2 to 10 run in parallel and never wait for stage 1's approval count.*" In Pull request rules, write "two, counted by a stage 1 job that reruns on each review and gates only merge". To stay within the 4000-word maximum (the verifier currently counts 3999), cut the same number of words elsewhere, for example "; the toolchain waits for OQ-repository-layout-and-conventions-3" in Scope (the OQ table already says it) and "(including the Semantic Cache vector client)" in Where Go code goes.

blocking.section: CI stages (stage 5 row and the note below the table)
blocking.issue: This revision added the `netgo,osusergo` tags to race runs. The next sentence says stage 5 "passes no `-tags`", so the two sentences now contradict each other. The stage 5 row also runs only `go test -race` in the release and floor jobs. On linux, `-race` needs cgo, so no job tests the `CGO_ENABLED=0` configuration that actually ships. Testing and quality strategy, which owns the pipelines, requires a second pr-fast job that runs the same tests without `-race` under `CGO_ENABLED=0` "so the shipped configuration is tested". An implementer who follows `make test` as specified here would build a race-only suite and leave that gap.

Line 455: "`go test -race -shuffle=on ./...` in the release and floor jobs, with identical JSON golden files".
